extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text, or span, from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Rajpurkar, P., Zhang, J., Lopyrev, K., & Liang, P. (2016). SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. arXiv preprint arXiv:1606.05250v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection occurred in three stages: curating Wikipedia passages, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs on those passages using crowdworkers who formulated questions in their own words and highlighted answer spans, and obtaining additional answer spans from other crowdworkers for the development and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Top 10,000 articles of English Wikipedia based on Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks, uniformly sampled to 536 articles.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual paragraphs were extracted from sampled Wikipedia articles, stripping away images, figures, and tables, and discarding any paragraphs shorter than 500 characters, yielding 23,215 paragraphs partitioned into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions per paragraph by entering questions in a text field and highlighting answer spans in the text, guided by sample paragraphs, good/bad examples, reminder prompts, and disabled copy-paste functionality. For development and test sets, secondary crowdworkers independently selected the shortest answering span for each question or submitted with no answer if unanswerable.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was evaluated on development and test sets by treating the second answer to each question as human prediction and the others as ground truth, yielding 77.0% exact match and 86.8% F1 on the test set. Mismatch occurred mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 answer per question in the training set; at least 3 answers per question in the development and test sets.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers located in the United States or Canada with a 97% HIT acceptance rate and a minimum of 1000 HITs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Answers are restricted to spans within a single reading passage rather than open-domain or interpretative answers found in advanced standardized tests, and candidate span accuracy may be bounded when answers do not align with constituency parse spans.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of machine comprehension and question answering models.
